abstract: The distribution of glycoconjugates in germ cells during spermatogenic differentiation, in carcinoma-in-situ (CIS) cells and in seminoma were studied by lectin histochemistry. The results show that human germ cells are rich in carbohydrate-containing compounds with specific alterations in the expression of glucosyl moieties during germ cell development. CIS cells reveal different lectin binding sites from spermatogenic cells, but the distribution of glycosubstances in CIS cells is similar to that of seminoma cells which supports the suggestion of the malignant nature of CIS germ cells.
abstract_ja: ヒトの胚細胞は、精子形成の分化過程で糖鎖を含む化合物に富み、グルコシル部分の発現に特異的な変化を示す。精細管内上皮内癌(CIS)細胞は精子形成細胞とは異なるレクチン結合部位を示したが、CIS細胞における糖質の分布はセミノーマ細胞と類似していた。これは、CIS胚細胞が悪性であるとの示唆を支持する。
